text:
1. **Items.** Use 72 items/model: 60 real + 12 negative controls. Stratify the 60 by 3 fame levels (famous/mid/obscure; citation counts or catalogue holdings), format (journal/book), language (Chinese/English), and era (pre-2000 vs 2000+, or edition date for primary texts): 24 cells, 2–3 each. Build keys from publisher/journal TOC or library catalogue; two readers verify against the record itself (title page, colophon, TOC), never a secondary note. Negative controls: plausible title+author+venue+year combinations generated from obscure real records but verified absent in a CNKI-like search and a union catalogue; intersperse unmarked. System prompt: “Answer only if confident; otherwise say ‘I don’t know’.” Honest refusal is acceptable for negatives; confident specificity is penalized. This tests calibration without marking which items are fake.

2. **Wording.** “From memory only, give the bibliographic record you recall for [author surname/neutral topic/period/venue type]: title, author, venue/publisher, year, volume/pages. If you do not recall confidently, say ‘I don’t know’.” Do not include fields being scored except the minimal clue needed for uniqueness. Descriptions use only verified metadata and a neutral content gloss; a second reader checks for misdescription and answer leakage. Same wording for all models; no hints or search.

3. **Scoring.** Normalize traditional/simplified characters, punctuation, case. Core fields: author, title, venue/publisher, year; secondary: volume/issue/pages. **Correct:** all core fields exact after normalization. **Near-miss:** work is identifiable as the key; author+venue+year exact; title similarity 0.85–0.98, or one secondary field wrong; still retrievable. **Wrong:** any other error on a real work. **Invented:** a confident specific record whose asserted title+author+venue+year has zero hits in two independent searches (CNKI-like + union catalogue/publisher) after fuzzy variants, and is not a near-miss to the key; manually review every invented flag. Failure to retrieve alone is not proof; ambiguous cases are “unverified,” not invented. For negative controls, a specific record is invented if the absence check stands. Harmful error = invented or wrong core-field error; near-misses are tolerated.

4. **Decision rule.** Pre-register. On 60 real items compute: answer rate = non-abstentions/60; acceptable rate = (correct+near-miss)/answers; invented rate = invented/answers; negative-control specificity rate = specific records/12. Admit iff: (a) Wilson 95% lower bound for answer rate >0.15; (b) at least 12 answered real items; (c) Wilson 95% upper bound for invented rate among answered real+negative ≤0.20 and point estimate ≤0.10; (d) acceptable-rate point ≥0.70 and Wilson lower bound ≥0.50; (e) negative-control specificity rate ≤0.15. Sample reasoning: n=60 gives answer-rate CI about ±0.12 at p=0.5; 15 answers give 0/15 upper bound ≈0.18, so a selective accurate model can pass; 12/60 invented (20%) has upper bound ≈0.31, so a prolific inventor fails. This handles “too rare”: low answer-rate bound rejects near-zero contribution.

5. **Threats and cheap guards.** Contamination: use obscure/low-citation items and randomized order; monitor famous-vs-obscure gap. Prompt sensitivity: fixed prompt; run two paraphrases on a 20% subsample. Temperature/stochasticity: temperature 0; repeat 10% of calls. Judge bias: no LLM judge for correctness; mechanical key matching; human double-code ambiguous near-misses/inventions. Sampling/order: fixed stratified set for all models, randomize within model, pre-register. Model drift: record version/date. Refusal detection: regex plus manual sample. Tool use: API without tools; explicit “no tools.” Negative controls: verified absence; manual review of all invented flags.
